docs.title: For management
docs.text: You: engineering, product, or delivery leadership rolling out a durable knowledge habit. Success: one owned repo, PR discipline, optional local RAG—without a separate wiki budget or vendor lock-in for assistants.

docs.title: Elevator pitch
docs.text:
Groundline keeps agreed know-how in git as Markdown. Anything merged to main is official. A local retrieval layer lets coding assistants cite that corpus instead of inventing from generic training data.

Full brief: Leadership brief.

docs.title: What you are (and are not) buying
docs.text: In scope Out of scope (v1) Git-reviewed corpus, cross-role folders (technical, testing, functional, …) Storing secrets, PII, or ticket threads in the repo PR workflow, CI gates, optional draft → reviewed on merge Replacing mentorship or management Local HTTP API + optional MCP; assistant-agnostic Hosted multi-tenant SaaS knowledge product

docs.title: Rollout checklist (6 steps)
docs.text:
1. Approve template adoption — team owns their remote (§4.5).
  2. Protect main — PR required, status check test (Branch protection).
  3. Name owners — who reviews knowledge/ by area; use .github/CODEOWNERS if helpful.
  4. Pilot one area — one service or feature; avoid boiling the ocean.
  5. Tie to definition of done — short knowledge PRs when decisions or runbooks matter.
  6. Communicate to non-devs — How to use Groundline; they can edit via GitHub UI.

docs.title: Risks leaders should monitor
docs.text:
• Corpus rot — docs without review; mitigate with PRs and reviewed / legacy_reviewed status.
  • Secret leakage — train contributors: no credentials or ticket paste in knowledge/.
  • Scope creep — REQUIREMENTS is the contract; customize policy in your fork, not ad hoc tool forks.
  • Measurement — golden-query recall and corpus growth sketched in REQUIREMENTS §11; tune when volume justifies it.

docs.title: Multi-team / line of business
docs.text: Each LoB should have its own clone + remote (§4.6). Share read access via API or git; do not mix unrelated prose in one knowledge/ tree without owners.

docs.title: Where engineering continues the story
docs.text: For engineering — install, API, MCP. For product and For quality — how other roles contribute without running Python.

docs.title: For product
docs.text: You: product manager, business analyst, or functional owner. Success: durable intent, decisions, and acceptance context in knowledge/functional/ (and related areas)—reviewed like code, findable later—without installing Groundline locally.

docs.title: What you contribute
docs.text:
Good fit in the corpus Keep outside the repo Problem statements, scope, decisions in plain language Raw JIRA/Linear threads or ticket URLs Acceptance themes, release notes, “why we chose X” Secrets, customer PII, confidential contracts Links to public specs or marketing pages Copy-paste of internal tracker exports

Normative rule: REQUIREMENTS §3 — self-contained markdown only.

docs.title: How to participate (no Python required)
docs.text:
1. Read How to use Groundline (sections 1–4).
  2. Ask your team which folder to use — usually knowledge/functional/ or knowledge/delivery/.
  3. Edit on GitHub: branch → edit file → Pull Request.
  4. Request a reviewer who knows the feature area.
  5. After merge, the note is official on main (automation may mark draft → reviewed).

Front matter at the top of each file (title, area, status: draft) is filled in by you or a dev partner—see the template in any existing knowledge/**/*.md file in the repo.

docs.title: What “good” looks like
docs.text:
• Short and factual — what was decided, for whom, and what to verify in QA.
  • Stable titles — search and retrieval use headings and metadata.
  • Version or product scope when older decisions still matter (applies_to, legacy_reviewed—ask a dev editor if unsure).

docs.title: How assistants use your words
docs.text: When engineers run the local index, retrieval can surface your merged prose during implementation and test design—if it is on main and clearly written. You do not need to use AI tools yourself for that to help.

python3 -m ki --root . status

docs.title: Golden queries (regression radar)
docs.text:
Defined in meta/golden_queries.yaml. Each query asserts recall@k and reports MRR@k (first-hit rank) against an expected doc_path substring.

python3 -m ki --root . index
python3 -m ki --root . status
python3 scripts/golden_queries.py --root .
python3 -m ki --root . eval --report md

When CI fails:

  1. Fix the corpus or query wording first (preferred).
  2. Re-index locally, re-run script until PASS.
  3. See Testing and Cursor skill teamkm-golden-query-tuning in the repo.

docs.text: No credentials in test data write-ups, no ticket dumps, no production customer data—REQUIREMENTS §3.
